posts.cooked:
The full text description of DW Setback from this wiki http://sentinelswiki.com/index.php?title=Setback is:

> While things deteriorated more and more in Rook City, the heroes who regularly patrolled the failing city grew increasingly concerned about the disappearance of Mr. Fixer. Three of the those heroes joined forces: Expatriette, Setback, and Nightmist. They worked together to protect Rook City and to investigate the loss of their friend.

When Amanda told Pete that they were going to team up, he had reservations. Of course, he was excited to help, but that was exactly the problem. He knew how things go for him - he didn't want Dark Watch to have any major setbacks. Even still, you can't help if you don't try, and Pete was very good at trying. When working with Dark Watch, Setback often leads the charge. He likes getting up close and personal with his opponents and also far enough away from his allies that he can't accidentally trip them up. Though he does like to spend as much time with Amanda as possible....

The hero team known as Dark Watch has gone through a lot. They were originally formed by Expatriette, Setback, and NightMist who were seeking to uncover the truth behind the events of the death of their friend, Mister Fixer. So, it was a bit of a rough start that the first major threat to Dark Watch was a mystically revived Mister Fixer! They managed to survive and even helped him reconnect his mind and body, so Mister Fixer became the fourth member of Dark Watch, fighting alongside those who risked everything to save him.

Based on that, I'm thinking something like Setback in the lead, along with Nightmist and Exp (possibly with someone in between them), but I'm curious about how to work in the Mister Fixer thing.  Part of me says he shouldn't be on the team, but another part says that we need to work in the resurrection somehow.  Hmmm.

From the wiki regarding DW Fixer

> The hero team known as Dark Watch has gone through a lot. They were originally formed by Expatriette, Setback, and NightMist who were seeking to uncover the truth behind the events of the death of their friend, Mister Fixer. So, it was a bit of a rough start that the first major threat to Dark Watch was a mystically revived Mister Fixer! They managed to survive and even helped him reconnect his mind and body, so Mister Fixer became the fourth member of Dark Watch, fighting alongside those who risked everything to save him.

What they found, however, was not exactly what they were looking for. They learned of the death of Mr. Fixer at the hand of his old pupil, The Operative, but his corpse had been sent to the fabled Temple of Zhu Long. The three heroes fought their way to that temple, only to be forced to face in combat the very subject of their search. A resurrected Mr. Fixer who knew not the faces or voices of his former allies fought them at the command of the mystical Zhu Long. In the course of the battle, NightMist managed to reconnect Mr. Fixer’s mind to his body, and the four escaped the temple together.

Now, Mr. Fixer fights as part of Dark Watch. There is much unknown about how he returned, and his body seems to be healthier and stronger than before, but he still experiences great, undying rage. He is a harsher combatant than ever before, and the other members of Dark Watch keep their eyes on Mr. Fixer, both concerned for his safety as well as their own.

So if we assume that the Operative death thing has already happened via the DW Fixer unlock, then maybe something like having Setback, Exp, Nightmist, and Fixer on the team, maybe have Fixer die and get resurrected? And then maybe after that Nightmist plays Enlightenment on him? (It's about the only helpful thing Nightmist can do to someone else, and it says she reconnected him).  Obviously you'd need Temple of Zhu Long, but maybe the villain wouldn't matter?  I mean, sure, you could say it has to be Chairman so Operative can kill Fixer, but again, seems like you're redoing DW Fixer at that point.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Here's how I did it:

Fixer last. 

Restart game until the first villain card play is prison break. 

If expat starts with no guns, restart game.

if fixer starts with no tools, restart game.

Setback provides ongoings for fixer. Generally provides damage, healing, redirection  

If possible, put nightmist into mist form ASAP. Otherwise use Oblivions to clear minions. 

Expat shoots stuff. 

Fixer uses Jack handle (if he has one) or dual crowbars (if he has them). If he has neither, restart game. 

Abuse the rewind feature with nightmist. If you reveal the wrong thing, rewind. 

It still requires luck, but setting up the initial conditions makes it a lot easier. You just need to be willing to restart the fight a lot.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
On Dark Watch Fixer by himself - Mr. FIxer is generally the most effective when he has a tool and a style in play when he attacks. Ideally you want Harmony as well. So, round 1 you play a style or a tool and do nothing. Round 2 you play a style or a tool and destroy one, assuming you have a replacement. If you destroy Driving Mantis you’ve lost all the benefit of the style, if you destroy Pipe Wrench you’ve lost the defensive benefit. Destroying Jack Handle or Dual Crowbars usually means playing a much weaker tool, since those are usually his strongest weapons. Destroying Tire Iron’s not so bad - unless you’re up against a villain who deploys a lot of 4-5 health targets. Dark Watch Fixer often can’t use Harmony at all, but getting Harmony out isn’t that common.

So, kind of weak, but not necessarily as bad as my knee-jerk reaction to self-destruction. The benefit is that his attack goes from a weak plink (1 point) to something that can plow through most defenses (3 points).

On combos with heroes who have benefits from card destruction - this isn’t that common, but fair point. It’s true that a number of Stuntman’s cards say “you get to do this significant thing on destruction,” regardless of what triggers the destruction. Some of KNYFE’s cards say that too. Mainstay I don’t know, since I’ve never played the physical game, so I only know his character from The Sentinels.

I have no idea if this has been pointed out before, so apoligies for redundancies. My strategy that eventually worked was to lock the Chairman and Rook City's decks. It's not as reliable as Dual Crowbar/Friendly Fire, but I was too impatient to reset until I got that hand, so this happened accidently. Basically, this is more something to just keep in mind as a longshot possibility.

Incap DW Mr. Fixer puts an envrionment card from trash on bottom of deck. Incap DW Nightmist puts the top card of a trash on top of it's deck.

It's possible, however unlikely it sounds, to engineer a case where the environment deck is near empty and The Chairman plays Perfect Human Specimines. As long as those envrionment cards aren't Scum and Villiany, and you deal with the Chairman's damaging targets, you can force a hard lock. Nightmist puts the PHS back on top of Chairman's deck every turn, and Fixer alternates Tony and Tremada on the bottom of the envrionment deck, since they will keep getting destroyed by the Villain Character cards.

From here, Setback can generate tokens and heal himself back to safety, and Expat can just play every single card ever. Then, whenever you want, build up setback's token pool and one-shot the operative and chairman. 

This all sounds pie in the sky rediculous, but I've made it work 3 times- my Steam, my brother's Steam, and my phone, out of proably 10  or 11 total games attempted. It's tedious, but safe, and you get a feel pretty quick if this setup is going to be possible. (Early prison breaks and scum/villany are your friends.)

posts.cooked:
Maybe that’s not as hard as it sounds at first. Neither condition (Perfect Human Specimens last played, Tony and Dr. Tremada are the only cards in the environment deck) really relies on chance.

Assume both are are incapacitated. Any time Tony or Dr. Tremada is in the trash, Mr. Fixer puts them back. Eventually the environment will be only those 2 cards. Any time the Chairman plays Perfect Human Specimens, Nightmist puts that back. Unless the environment forces another Chairman play, or an Informant plays a Chairman card, the Chairman is locked into playing that card forever. The Operative will shuffle the Chairman’s deck every turn, but that happens after they play Perfect Human Specimens.

The main issue is that the Operative will still play all the underbosses, so you need to deal with each of them in turn. You can assume that Jailbreak is put on hold forever, so they won’t come back once you get rid of them.

Informants and Scum and Villany are both a problem because they can break the Perfect Human Specimens lock. Twisting Back Alleys can also break it, but it’s destroyable before it takes effect.

posts.cooked: Worth noting also that once you have a lock in place, or are very close, Twisted Back Alley and Blighted Streets do nothing and don’t need to be destroyed.
